data.rationale: Scenario-owned durable data observed in the canonical data directory.

budget.rationale: Durable storage is bounded by the workload byte ceiling; it is alarm-only because the data is not regenerable.

storage.rationale: Storage surfaces are declared from observed canonical scenario directories; external resource databases are not claimed by this scenario.

service.name: device-sync-hub
service.description: Polished, secure cross-device file and text transfer hub: push files or text from any trusted device and pull them on your other devices, relayed through your always-on server.

scenario-authenticator.degraded_behavior: If scenario-authenticator is unavailable, device-sync-hub fails closed in production: no pairing, no token validation, no access to items. Its own test lifecycle is not gated on the sibling's health.
scenario-authenticator.description: Owner identity, JWT (access + refresh), token validation, session list, and immediate revocation. Consumed over HTTP; device-sync-hub owns the device/pairing/trust/presence/per-item-ACL layer on top of it and does not extend the authenticator.

redis.purpose: Optional: brief caching of auth-token validations and cross-instance device presence. Single-server deployments degrade gracefully to in-memory presence; metadata persists in SQLite via api-core/storage, not Redis.

tier-1-local.notes: Optional accelerator that no Go code in this scenario currently opens. The declaration records intended caching, not a runtime requirement.

tier-2-desktop.reason: No vendorable cross-platform RESP server exists
tier-2-desktop.notes: The scenario does not require Redis, so the desktop tier simply runs without it rather than shipping a server.

swappable_with.notes: A durable local store behind the same Store seam preserves the durability property across restart, but not cross-replica sharing. A deployment running more than one replica still needs a real Redis.
